newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian 10-year bond support holds for now.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian 10-year bond support holds for now.

text.p: *Australian 10-year bond futures survived an assault of key support at 92.850, although the bullish sentiment of recent weeks has become slightly tarnished.
*Wage bargaining agreements seen as next test for market.
Australian 10-year bond futures survived a test of key support at 92.850, although the bullish sentiment of recent weeks has become slightly tarnished.

Monday's strong quarterly capital expenditure (capex) report was one of the first signs that the economy may be pulling out of its soft patch, denting hopes that the Reserve Bank will need to ease monetary conditions again, analysts said.

The next key test for the local market is likely to be the latest report on enterprise bargianing agreements, which is expected to emerge in the next few days, and which is another piece of data the RBA is keeping a close watch on.

"If that's showing the underlying increase is above 5.0 percent, then rather like the data we had yesterday, it will just erode the market again," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.

The local short end was notably weaker in morning trading on waning hopes of an imminent cut in official interest rates and as the Australian dollar finally succumbed to a partial correction after last week's heady rise against the U.S. dollar, although this proved short lived.
Three-year bond yields backed up to around 6.50 percent, the current level of official interest rates.

The market's late recovery saw the Australian/U.S. 10-year margin pull back below 100 basis points. However, the most notable move was against the New Zealand market, which outperformed the dollar bloc, triggered by a successful T-bond tender. The 10-year N.Z. spread to Australia went to a discount.

The 92.850 level on the 10-year contract represented a near three-month upward trendline from around 91.700 seen in early September, although this now moves up to 92.860 going into the after hours session. -- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
